Composite-Likelihood Cox Model with a Ridge Penalty (Individual-Level External Data)

cox_indi_ridge.Rd

Fits the composite-likelihood Cox model of cox_indi, in which the internal rows carry weight 1 and the rows of an external individual-level cohort carry weight \(\eta\), with a ridge (L2) penalty on the coefficients, over a path of penalty values for each \(\eta\).

Usage

cox_indi_ridge(
  z_int,
  delta_int,
  time_int,
  stratum_int = NULL,
  z_ext,
  delta_ext,
  time_ext,
  stratum_ext = NULL,
  etas,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 100,
  penalty.factor = 0.999,
  standardize = TRUE,
  tol = 1e-07,
  max_iter = 100,
  message = FALSE,
  ties = c("none", "breslow")
)

Arguments

z_int, delta_int, time_int, stratum_int

Internal covariate matrix, event indicator, observed times and optional strata.

z_ext, delta_ext, time_ext, stratum_ext

The same for the external cohort, with the same covariates in the same column order.

etas

Non-negative weights of the external rows.

lambda

Optional ridge penalty values. If NULL, a path of nlambda values is generated for each \(\eta\), ending at 0.

nlambda

Number of penalty values when lambda is NULL. Default 100.

penalty.factor

Numeric in [0, 1); the largest penalty of the generated path is the null-model score divided by 1 - penalty.factor, as for coxkl_ridge. Default 0.999.

standardize

Logical. Scale the stacked design to unit standard deviation before penalising. Default TRUE.

tol, max_iter

Convergence tolerance on the Newton step and the iteration limit.

message

Logical. Print a progress bar.

ties

"none" or "breslow", as in cox_indi.

Value

An object of class "cox_indi_ridge": eta (the weights), lambda (a list, one penalty path per \(\eta\)), beta (a list of \(p \times L\) coefficient matrices on the original scale), linear.predictors_int (a list of \(n_{int} \times L\) matrices in the caller's row order), ties and data.

Details

For each \(\eta\) the function maximises on the per-observation scale of the ridge family, i.e. \([\ell_{int}(\beta) + \eta\,\ell_{ext}(\beta)] / n_{eff} - \tfrac{1}{2}\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2\) with \(n_{eff}\) the larger of the total weight and the number of rows (the denominator of cox_indi_enet), by Newton–Raphson with step halving, along a decreasing \(\lambda\) path with warm starts. The two cohorts sit in strata of their own, so no risk set mixes them. The penalty is applied on the scale of the standardised design when standardize = TRUE (scaling by the standard deviation of the stacked design, no centering), and the coefficients are returned on the original scale. At \(\lambda = 0\) the fit is the one of cox_indi.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(ExampleData_indi)
fit <- cox_indi_ridge(
  z_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$z, delta_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$status,
  time_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$time,
  z_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$z, delta_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$status,
  time_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$time,
  etas = c(0, 0.5, 1))
} # }
